## Exhaustibility (XA-c/d)

Anchors (operator-supplied, echoed for the certificate): nodes/sec = 1.5e+09, hedge = x2, work factor = x1, wall-clock ceiling = 1e+12 h. Effective rate band = 7.5e+08 .. 3e+09 nodes/sec (slow end = nodes/sec / (work factor x hedge), fast end = nodes/sec x hedge / work factor). Note: rate rounded up from the d3 11.2T canonical run (11.2e12 nodes in 7,810 s on one D128als_v7; documentation/CANONICAL_HASHES.md); ceiling chosen to be generous; TR-12 section 3

Branches ascending by node cost. The hedge is a band on the rate: a row reads
EXHAUSTIBLE only if its cost at the SLOW end of the band fits the ceiling,
INFEASIBLE only if its cost at the FAST end exceeds it, and UNDECIDED:hedge
between the two.  `wall/ceiling` is the shortfall factor at each
end; on an INFEASIBLE row its fast-end value is the least the shortfall can
be.  The verdict column and the shortfall are computed in EXACT rational
arithmetic from the exact 192-bit t-unit counts and the operator's typed
decimal anchors; the `wall (h)` and `wall/ceiling` NUMERALS
are 4-significant-digit decimal renderings of those exact values, for
reading only.  Do not re-derive a verdict from the printed numerals -- at
the boundary a binary64 round trip is enough to reverse the call.  The
`wall (h) exact` columns are the exact rational costs themselves.
